memory_update.text: MKSI should be carried forward as the strongest US-listed underfollowed proxy for FC-BGA/package-substrate process chemistry via Atotech; verify AI/ABF/FC-BGA materiality in filings and calls.

CAMT should be carried forward as a mid-cap yield-inspection hypothesis for advanced packaging and possibly substrate-related inspection; survival requires evidence separating package-substrate exposure from general advanced-packaging/HBM inspection.

ONTO should be tracked as a larger-cap process-control and inspection candidate with AI advanced-packaging exposure, but its direct FC-BGA substrate-material linkage is weaker than MKSI and needs application-level confirmation.

For this node, US-listed names are mostly second-order process enablers rather than the dominant materials suppliers; the clean dominant suppliers cited in seed evidence are Ajinomoto for insulating film and MEC for copper adhesion chemistry.

Need a non-US-listed parallel map for Ajinomoto, MEC, Ibiden, Unimicron, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Nan Ya PCB, Shinko, and regional second-source chemistry/laminate suppliers before ranking the global chokepoint.

node: FC-BGA package substrate materials, insulating film, and copper adhesion chemistry
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a narrow US-listed universe with plausible exposure to FC-BGA substrate materials, copper/plating chemistry, substrate/process inspection, and advanced-packaging execution. The cleanest direct US-listed mapping is not the dominant insulating-film or copper-adhesion suppliers cited in the seed evidence, because Ajinomoto and MEC are not clean US-listed AI chip plays. Instead, the US-listed candidates cluster around wet-chemistry/process equipment, inspection/metrology for advanced substrates and packages, and OSAT packaging capacity. MKS/Atotech and Camtek are the strongest underfollowed-lane candidates for this specific node; Onto and Amkor are useful context/adjacent names but less hidden or less material-specific.
